title: Leadership convergence: cross-team staff standup notes — 2027-08-10
content:
Attendees: Aisha (chair), Jonas, Liang, Maya, Ravi, Ellen, plus SRE representative (Carlos) for the first 20 minutes.

Purpose: quick cross-team alignment on operational risks, rollout pacing, and blockers that need leadership support. Keep to 45 minutes.

AGENDA (ordered by risk & timeline):
1) Canary rollout for 2.3.1 kernel selection change (KV cache refactor).
2) Production latency p95 regression observed in eu-west-1 (last 48h).
3) Dedicated capacity queueing policy update and pricing/throughput tradeoffs.
4) Staging test flakiness preventing release gating for private deployments.
5) Hiring/triage: SRE oncall ramp and support for holiday coverage.
6) Quick wins / blockers and escalations.

SUMMARY NOTES / DISCUSSION POINTS:
- 2.3.1 KV cache refactor: Liang summarized the diff and the motivation (reduce memory churn, improve prefix-caching hit rate). Initial canary at 0.5% yesterday showed improved p50 but a small p95 regression on long-sequence workloads using large-decoder models. Hypothesis: kernel selection falls back to slower matmul path for sequences >1024 when quantization profile mismatched.
  - Jonas: metric signal lines up with the A100v5 kernel mismatch we saw in bench harness.
  - Maya: only affects a subset of customer queries (long-context chat sessions).
  - Agree to pause broad rollout until a patch is ready.

Decision: rollback automatic promotion; keep 0.5% canary frozen. Do not expand to 5% until patch validated in our perf harness and canary stable for 48h.

- eu-west-1 p95 increase: Carlos presented SLO telemetry (last 48h) showing p95 +18% for generation endpoints. Root causes identified: (1) transient storage latency on prefix cache store (S3 proxy timeout spikes), and (2) a routing skew that sent more long-context requests to a subset of hosts because autoscaler lagged during a small traffic shift.
  - Short term mitigation: increase cache store connection pool and temporarily route long-context traffic across regions with lower tail latency (policy change, 1 hour).
  - Medium term: software retry/backoff improvements for prefix cache store and change autoscaler cooldowns for bursty traffic patterns.

- Dedicated capacity queueing policy: Product asked for clearer throughput SLA options for customers (burst vs reserved). Ravi ran numbers: current reserved pools deliver X tokens/sec per GPU at 90th percentile; burst capacity can add ~35% for short windows but impacts latency SLOs at high fill. Need clearer pricing buckets.
  - Action: Finance + Product + Platform to draft 3 pricing/guarantee tiers (Reserved, Elastic, Guaranteed Burst) by next Friday.

- Staging flakiness blocking private deployment release: test failures intermittently reproducible locally but not in canary. Failures in e2e acceptance around routing persistence layer. Ellen and SRE suggested adding deterministic failpoints to reproduce race condition.
  - Temporary mitigation: add more conservative timeout gates and mark the failing test as flaky while we root cause.

- Hiring & oncall: SRE headcount gap of 1.5 FTE during Sep-Oct window. Need part-time contractors to cover peak.
  - Agreement: People Ops to open short posting for 60–90 day oncall contractor; SRE to shortlist by next Tuesday.

QUICK WINS CALLED OUT: 
- Observability: add per-request kernel selector telemetry to better correlate p95 spikes with kernel decisions (Jonas owns instrumentation plan).
- Cost: inexpensive caching layer tweak (reduce prefix cache expiry from 5m to 90s for low-variance workloads) could reduce cold miss storm; Maya to validate in staging.

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS FOR LEADERSHIP: 
- Customer communication: do we proactively notify customers on Dedicated who may be impacted by kernel mismatch (long-context customers) or wait until patch? Product prefers proactive note for customers who have private peering / dedicated appliances.
- Capacity across regions: if eu-west-1 is increasingly noisy, what's the tolerance for cross-region routing of low-compliance workloads? Security & compliance team input required.

DECISIONS (explicit):
- Pause expansion of 2.3.1 kernel patch beyond 0.5% canary. (owner: Liang)
- Implement short-term routing redistribution for eu-west-1 for long-context requests. (owner: Carlos / SRE)
- Draft Dedicated pricing tiers and throughput guarantees for next leadership review. (owner: Ravi + Product: Maya)
- Add per-request kernel selector telemetry to observability backlog. (owner: Jonas)

ACTION ITEMS (concrete, prioritized):
1) Liang: push kernel-selection patch to bench harness and validate against long-sequence perf tests. Target: 2027-08-12.
2) Carlos (SRE): enact temporary routing change and cache pool increase; monitor p95; report back in 6 hours once in effect.
3) Jonas: instrument kernel selector telemetry; submit PR for observability dashboard and a short runbook for how to read the signal. Target: 2027-08-13.
4) Maya + Ravi + Finance: draft 3-tier Dedicated offering with slate of guarantees and suggested price deltas. Target: 2027-08-17.
5) Ellen + QA: add deterministic failpoints to reproduce staging e2e flake and open a bug ticket with reproduction steps. Target: 2027-08-14.
6) People Ops + SRE leads: post & shortlist oncall contractor candidates. Target shortlist: 2027-08-11.

STATUS TRACKING TABLE (informal):
- 2.3.1 canary: frozen at 0.5% (status: paused)
- eu-west-1 p95 mitigation: in-flight (status: emergency mitigation)
- Dedicated pricing: scoping (status: drafting)
- Staging e2e flake: triage (status: investigating)
- Oncall coverage: hiring (status: urgent)

NOTES TO SELF / FOLLOW-UPS:
- Leadership requested a one-pager for customers on how we handle kernel/quantization fallbacks; could be used for proactive comms. (assign to Aisha for draft)
- Add a short incident postmortem template to reduce friction when a region has repeated tail latency spikes; tie to playbook.

NEXT MEETING: 2027-08-17, 09:00 PT. Focus: canary status, eu-west-1 metric feedback, Dedicated pricing draft review.

Raw meeting chatter / scratch (kept for context):
- Jonas: "bench harness shows the fallthrough path is 12–18% slower with current quant profiles."
- Liang: "I want to be conservative — customer impact > perf win not worth it yet."
- Maya: "Product wants to avoid surprise bill shock if we tighten Reserved vs Burst rules."

End of notes.
